correctness.rationale: The 24-arc complex has a completely exhausted finite face poset (1816 faces), with agreement of two independent enumeration methods; 835 exact matched face pairs form a globally acyclic Hasse matching, and 835 signed integer unit cancellations preserve integral chain homotopy. Sole reduced boundary is 12 by 101 with nine unit pivots and zero residual, producing free ranks 3,92,32 in dimensions 2,3,4. Direct complete mod-two boundary ranks (23,169,444,208) and Euler characteristic agree. No infinite or homotopy-wedge inference is made.

evidence: arXiv:2208.04656 treats linear, polygonal, grid and transitive-tournament complexes and a generating function for one-way complete bipartite orientations. The previously recorded universal Hamiltonian-cycle top-degree theorem applies here and predicts the rank 32 in degree four but does not specify degrees two and three.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general top-degree theorem is strictly partial coverage, not a claim of new rank 32; no general complete lower-degree formula for all tripartite bidirected digraphs was found. Different bipartite or tree families cannot imply exact homology for a nonbipartite octahedral graph.

evidence: Vrećica and Živaljević (2007), arXiv:0710.5252, identify multipath complexes of fully bidirected complete digraphs with cycle-free chessboard complexes; this object is the subcomplex obtained from Omega_6 by deleting six rook vertices for three opposite pairs. Their theorems concern connectivity of the full or other constructed complexes, not this exact deletion.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Cycle-free chessboard is a true alternate name/model, not a different invariant. Passing to this particular induced subcomplex changes the chain complex. No inspected stronger exact computation of this induced deletion establishes its lower integral homology.

originality.rationale: The exact lower integral groups in degrees two and three, including torsion-freeness, are not implied by inspected multipath calculations for linear graphs, polygons, transitive tournaments, bidirected double stars, or complete bipartite graphs. Universal top-homology Hamiltonian-cycle result already implies rank 32 in degree four; this covered part is openly identified and does not constitute the new contribution. The complete 12-by-101 integer boundary at this distinct graph is a substantive uncovered computation, with unindexed-equivalence risk acknowledged.
residual_risks: Some older or unindexed cycle-free-chessboard deletion computation may contain an equivalent exact result; searches cannot establish uniqueness.

value.rationale: The octahedral K2,2,2 graph is the smallest balanced tripartite simple graph with nontrivial parts and a canonical symmetric nonbipartite example. The complete lower-degree integral multipath homology, mixed three-degree support, and absence of torsion answer a natural exact topology question beyond tree/cycle/bipartite classifications. It is not merely the already-known top-degree Hamiltonian-cycle count, and no unproved generalization is asserted.
